status: Final eight Grade 6 duties reviewed through existing claims; own-community change and its overall closure retain explicit unbound-local-resource Partials.

buxton.readScope: Complete main heritage/history body, reread 11 November 2026.
facts: The 1849 refugee settlement developed farms, homes, institutions and education; later 1859 facilities are separately dated.
The site was nationally designated in 1999; surviving landscape and institutions are described as a continuing memorial/community.
buxton.limits: Use the actual time layers. Do not turn promotional heritage judgments into a claim racism ended or that every present resident shares one identity.

port-royal.readScope: Actual introduction and 1603–1607 settlement/main institutional history, reread 11 November 2026.
facts: A fur-trade monopoly with settlement and missionary conditions supported a French expedition; commercial, colonial and religious aims are distinct.
Mi’kmaq expertise/relationships mattered, and later conflict and withdrawal cannot be erased by describing commercial opportunity.
port-royal.limits: Not every worker had the same personal motive. Exclude the source’s first-settlement superlative, romantic discovery narrative and unsupported all-Europe religious-tolerance comparison.

collaboration-2017.readScope: Complete main body, especially Collaborative work; historical not current-pending legislation.
facts: The account identifies a 2017 co-development process involving Canadian Heritage, the Assembly of First Nations, Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami and the Métis Nation.
It states a distinctions-based approach rather than treating all Indigenous languages/contexts as identical.
collaboration-2017.limits: An attributed federal account of collaboration, not every person’s consent, present representatives or proof all proposed goals were achieved. Outdated broad language-endangerment statistics are not used.

facts: The Act received Royal Assent on 21 June 2019 and is intended to support language reclamation/maintenance/strengthening.
The account describes a collaborative development/engagement process.
legislation-2019.limits: Enactment/engagement are institutional steps, not evidence every language recovered or every person/community agreed or experienced equal inclusion.

Evidence from the Past: identify surviving evidence, infer a supported use/user from an old object/photo, and explain why fewer surviving records limit knowledge. Own-community comparison adds a source-specific task; the whole claim is not reduced to spotting two dates.
wholeClaimReview.readiness: All old hard supports/whole vocabulary or observation operations remain unchanged and unassumed. No fabricated prerequisite associations, age-floor lowering or automatic whole mastery from component tasks.
wholeClaimReview.excluded: Australia-specific migration and community-change claims retain their Australian knowledge. No Canadian copy or silent rewrite is made.

preparedLocalProtocol.workedExample: Use the actual Love Park project account at the bound resource: former off-ramp removal 2016–17, construction July 2021–June 2023, opening June 2023, documented retained trees/new planting/path/public-space change. The provider’s account supports physical/documentary change, not measured visitor, health or ecological benefits.
ownCommunityPreparation: Adult verifies an ordinary actual community in Canada to which the learner belongs, such as their local town/region or school community, without collecting a private home address. Select an actual publicly documented change and at least two dated records: before/transition and later/current account or observation.

Prepare attributed source extracts and an old object/photo or publicly documented feature with legible contextual clues. Record place, date, creator and evidence type; where the earlier record does not establish a fact, mark it unknown. Do not invent a cultural-group history to match a pupil’s appearance.

The Toronto worked case models the procedure but only meets own-community application when it genuinely is the learner’s selected community. Otherwise use the same bounded schema for the actual local case; absence of a particular packet is an explicit delivery condition, not fabricated completion.
actions: Use the actual old source’s clues to infer a supported past use/user, explain why that inference rests on surviving evidence and why missing records limit what can be known. Compare the independently dated later record without assuming every difference was caused by one event.

Describe a significant actual change within the selected own community, what remained and why the evidence supports its significance; distinguish an actual physical/service/cultural change from an unmeasured benefit or a plan not yet delivered.
Present the own-community comparison with source/date/known/unknown annotations. Transfer to another public source detail: revise only the supported part, not copy the Toronto conclusion.
preparedLocalProtocol.positive: An actual own-community change is described with dated surviving evidence, supported old-use inference and a meaningful continuity/uncertainty distinction.
preparedLocalProtocol.nearMiss: Generic historical facts, a fictional local event, an unrelated worked case, a date with no described change or a promised outcome treated as measured.

actions: Actually compare documented motives in three distinct movements: French commercial/settlement/missionary enterprise in early Acadia; Black refugees seeking freedom/security at Buxton; Jewish refugees/survivors seeking escape from persecution and a later home in Canada. Use the actual source accounts, not a reason guessed from ethnicity.

Distinguish seeking refuge or opportunity from being admitted, and a colony’s official purpose from every person’s motive. The1939St.Louisrefusal and later survivor arrivals are different outcomes; do not say the ship docked in Canada or every passenger later immigrated.
Explain a supported effect of the migration interconnection and retain the separately assessed actual aid connection in the complete country-interconnections claim.
successEvidence: Different peoples’ main documented migration motives are explained with actual cases and relevant distinctions, rather than memorising all illustrative examples.
nearMisses: Every migrant moved for money, all newcomers chose freely, or every person with one identity had one motive.
migration-reasons.transfer: A fictional caption says all three groups came for an identical reason and were immediately welcomed. Correct it from the actual cases and name a personal motive the sources cannot establish.

actions: Analyse Black Buxton’s refugee community-building/education and Jewish Toronto’s hospital/community-care response as different settler/newcomer contributions. Explain the contribution-to-shared-life relationship rather than list a name or date.

Use Parks’ actual current commemorative framing of the Buxton landscape and the hospital’s service beyond its founders to discuss how freedom, education and care can contribute to Canadian public identities. Distinguish the learner’s supported analysis from a survey of what everyone believes.
Retain exclusion and unequal access alongside contribution: achievement did not earn rights and neither case proves a homogeneous or fully inclusive Canada.
successEvidence: Analyses actual contributions of more than one settler/newcomer group and supported Canadian identity relationships with limits.
nearMisses: Lists famous people without a contribution relationship or says community contributions prove equal access for everyone.
settler-contributions.transfer: Compare an original claim that only one group built Canadian community life with the two actual cases; explain supported plurality without making every community or person identical.

actions: Explain the specific First Nations/ITK/Métis Nation contribution to the historical2017co-development process and distinguish the 2019 enactment from an old promise still pending. Use the actual distinctions-based account; no claim of unanimous agreement or universal representative authority.

Connect the actual community-led language renewal cases with belonging/participation and the Jewish community response to exclusion with wider care and protection. This actually includes First Nation, Métis AND Inuit communities rather than offering them as an unused list.

Assess the extent of inclusion using explicit criteria: recognition/protection, meaningful participation and actual access/outcomes are different. The source packet supports particular legal/institutional steps and community contributions; it cannot establish equal lived outcomes for all. Explain a reasoned, qualified judgment and what evidence would be needed for a nationwide outcome claim.

Retain actual Canadian protections and their scope/qualification distinctions. The fictional federal-service discrimination case tests a protection/complaint mechanism, not the frequency of current discrimination or a verdict in a real case.
successEvidence: Explains several actual contributions including all three Indigenous peoples, and assesses extent against stated criteria with supported progress and outcome-evidence limits.
nearMisses: Act passed therefore every language recovered, all people agreed, or Canada is fully inclusive.
Rights exist only for citizens or were earned through achievement.
inclusiveness.transfer: A fictional public poster claims that a law and a successful community institution prove discrimination has ended. Explain what the actual evidence establishes and which claim requires further lived-access/outcome evidence.

actions: Identify distinct studied First Nation, Métis and Inuit community cases, and Black/Jewish settler/community institutional cases, keeping people/place/period and historical versus contemporary settings distinct.

Explain supported contributions to Canadian development: place/transport/food/trade knowledge in the actual historical cases, continuing community language/knowledge transmission, and refugee settlement/education or care institutions. State how a contribution mattered; do not assign every member one occupation.

Compare more than one kind of community relationship, such as a regional kinship/trade network, a settlement and a contemporary cultural/education organization. An institution is not automatically an entire people or a municipal jurisdiction.
successEvidence: Various actual community types and specific supported contributions are identified and explained, without an exhaustive census or stereotype.
nearMisses: Treats every Indigenous community as one place or equates every organization with a sovereign government.
community-types.transfer: Use a fresh detail from one actual packet: identify the particular community relationship and supported contribution while saying what it does not establish about all Canadians.

actions: Identify and describe several fundamental elements with actual Canadian content: respect/protection for rights, distinct continuing First Nations/Métis/Inuit peoples and cultures, and the importance of particular treaty relationships. Explain them through the actual rights, renewal and actual verified territory/treaty worked cases.

Distinguish a shared public principle or institution from identical personal identities, universal lived inclusion or a legal title ruling. A treaty reference, traditional territory and reserve are not interchangeable. Canada’s diversity does not mean every Indigenous people is one culture or Métis identity is mixed ancestry alone.

Keep the complete rights and second-place treaty/territory distinction checks. These actual verified cases support the national-principle task without asserting they are every learner’s own community. The official examples illustrate a broader field; no full constitutional-office, health-system or symbol inventory is imported.
successEvidence: Describes several supported fundamental Canadian identity elements and actual relationships, retaining distinct peoples, rights scope and treaty/resource limits.
nearMisses: Recites generic kindness, replaces every territory with the nearest reserve, or assumes every Canadian has one personal identity.
canadian-identities.transfer: A fictional display merges all Indigenous peoples and claims rights depend on birthplace. Correct it with the actual learned Canadian principles and explain an appropriate source-bound treaty example.
